summary: Rows 30-35 are six linear, filler-free canon episodes that close the Baran (Destiny) arc and open the Holy Sword arc: in OUR chapter space they run ch 104 -> 125 (vols 12-14) at ~3.5 chapters per episode. The block's one real finding is a CHAPTER-SPACE FAULT LINE that this wave must handle series-wide: OUR catalog space (349 chapters; the stored v1-v37 table = en-WP's 'List of ... volumes') reserves slot 122 for the 番外編 'The Hero Avan' (V Jump, Nov 1991), printed at the end of tankobon vol 13, while dragonquest.fandom numbers only the 348 mainline chapters contiguously. So fandom N = OUR N for N <= 121 and fandom N = OUR N+1 for N >= 122. Every chapter the fandom prints from 'The Incident at the Finals!!' (fandom 122) onward must be +1'd before it becomes an anchor. Ep 35 is the first row in the run where this bites: the fandom's '121, 122, 123, 124 (partial)' is OUR '121, 123, 124, 125 (partial)' — the anime never adapts OUR 122 because it is the side story (it was adapted instead as the separate 'Yuusha Avan to Gokuen no Maou' manga, ch 1). Two fandom per-episode field defects were caught and repaired against the licensor: ep 34's forward field DROPS ch 118 and ADDS ch 121 (the reverse field and TV Tokyo's synopses put 118 in ep 34 and 121 in ep 35), and ch 112's reverse field credits 'ep 31 (Partial)' with no completing episode (the forward field and TV Tokyo put 112 whole in ep 32).

anchors.note: A10 START: ch 104 'The Dragonoid Awakens!!!' is split with ep 29, which holds only a leading partial (fandom ch-104 page: 'episode 29 (Partial), episode 30') — ep 30 holds the bulk, so START=104. A4 END: ep 30 runs into ch 108 'The Hero Dai's Revival!!!'; TV Tokyo's ep-31 synopsis OPENS on 'the dragon crest that surfaced on Dai's right fist', i.e. ch 108's beat already shown at ep 30's close, so the tail is a real share and A47's scrap test is not met (no page evidence either way; the series' stored convention, ep 12->44 and ep 16->57, advances the END on a marked partial). All numbers here are below 122 so the fandom, en-WP and OUR space coincide.

A10 START: ch 108 is split with ep 30; the fandom ch-108 page marks 'episode 30 (partial), episode 31' — ep 31 holds the bulk, START=108. A4 END: the episode's forward field stops at '111 (partial)' and TV Tokyo's ep-32 synopsis opens on ch-111 material (Dai has lost his weapon, Baran is out of magic power, Hyunckel entrusts him the Armour Sword), so ch 111 straddles 31/32 and ch 112 belongs to ep 32. MEDIUM because the fandom's ch-112 page credits 'episode 31 (Partial)' and names no episode that completes it — a self-inconsistent reverse field (see flags); en-WP ch 109 'The World's Ultimate Offense and Defense!!' matches the synopsis line 'the greatest battle on earth was about to begin'.

A10 START: the leading share of ch 111 is story-carrying, not a sliver — TV Tokyo's ep-32 synopsis leads with it (weapon lost, Baran out of magic, Hyunckel's Armour Sword) and the fandom ch-111 page marks both 'episode 31 (Partial), episode 32 (partial)' — so START=111. A4 END: ep 32 reaches into ch 114 'The Final Notice'; the episode's cast carries Vearn, Mystvearn, Killvearn, Hadlar and Zaboera (the Vearn-palace ultimatum, ch 114's opening) while ep 33's cast has Mystvearn only as a mention, so the palace scene sits here. Ep title 'Farewell to the Father' = ch 113 'A Father's Farewell' (chichi to no ketsubetsu) — an exact en-WP namesake. Below 122: fandom = en-WP = OUR space.

A10 START: ep 33 opens on the remainder of ch 114 — TV Tokyo: 'Hadlar, given a last chance by Vearn, sets out with Zaboera to kill Dai himself' — a story-carrying share, so START=114 (the fandom ch-114 page marks 'episode 32 (partial), episode 33 (partial)'). A4 END: clean at ch 117 'Individual Missions' (the fandom ch-117 page credits ep 33 alone and ep 34 starts a new chapter), so no C1 continue is owed. Ch 115 'Maam's Back...!!?' = the synopsis' 'an unexpected person appears before Popp' (the fake Maam). Below 122: fandom = en-WP = OUR space.

The fandom's FORWARD field on this page is defective in BOTH directions (the kingdom.fandom shape): it prints '119, 120, 121' — dropping ch 118 and adding ch 121. Ch 118 is restored by the fandom's own ch-118 page ('2020: episode 34') and by the episode's Manga-differences list, which discusses Baduck relaying Leona's orders to the Troika, the Papnica knives and the Sea Knife — ch 118 'Where's the Strongest Blade?' verbatim. Ch 121 is removed because the fandom's ch-121 page credits ep 35 alone AND TV Tokyo's ep-35 synopsis carries ch 121's content ('Maam promises the two she will win the Romos tournament and take the Blade of Champions'); ep 34's own item list has the Sword of Champions only as a '(mention)'. Ep title = ch 119 'The Romos Martial Arts Tournament' (en-WP namesake). MEDIUM: the forward/reverse conflict on the END is resolved by the licensor, not by two agreeing wiki fields.

SPACE CONVERSION APPLIED (see structure): the fandom's '121, 122, 123, 124 (partial)' is OUR 121, 123, 124, 125 (partial) — OUR slot 122 is the 番外編 'The Hero Avan', not a mainline chapter, and the anime does not adapt it. A10 START: ch 121 'The Blade of Champions' opens the episode (fandom ch-121 page credits ep 35 alone; TV Tokyo: 'Maam promises to win the tournament and obtain the Blade of Champions'). A4 END: OUR ch 125 'The Fearsome Hyper Demon' (en-WP + MangaDex agree on this number and title) is entered but not finished — TV Tokyo's ep-36 synopsis opens with Zamza ALREADY transformed into the hyper demon, and ep 35's Manga-differences already cover the Crest Beam exposing Zamza's chest mouth, so the share is substantial and A47's scrap test is not met. Ep title 'The Incident at the Finals' = OUR ch 123 'Disaster in the Finals!!' (kesshousen no ihen) — an exact en-WP namesake in OUR numbering, which is itself a check on the +1.

structure.notes: CHAPTER SPACE — the wave-level finding. OUR catalog space has total_chapters = 349 and the stored v1-v37 boundary table, which is exactly en.wikipedia's 'List of Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai volumes' original-release list (v1 1-9 ... v13 114-122, v14 123-132 ... v37 342-349). That list holds 348 numbered chapter TITLES and exactly one unlisted number, 122, at the END of volume 13 — the slot of the bangaihen 'The Hero Avan' (Yuusha Avan, V Jump Nov 1991), printed as a bonus at the back of tankobon vol 13. dragonquest.fandom numbers only the 348 MAINLINE chapters, contiguously. Hence: fandom N = OUR N for N <= 121; fandom N = OUR N + 1 for N >= 122. Three independent checks: (1) the fandom's 'The Hero Avan' page states its neighbours explicitly — 'previous: chapter 121 (tankobon ed.) ... next: chapter 122 (tankobon ed.)', i.e. the side story occupies the slot between mainline 121 and the next mainline chapter, which is OUR 122; (2) the fandom's own per-chapter |volume= fields agree with OUR stored table only under the +1 — fandom 122 'The Incident at the Finals!!' is marked volume 14, and 123 (OUR number) is the first chapter of OUR v14 (123-132); fandom 131 'Zamza, Fade Into the Setting Sun' is marked vol 14 and is OUR 132, v14's last; fandom 132 'A New Adventure!!!' is vol 15 and is OUR 133, v15's first (133-141); fandom 183 'Chikai no Masou' is vol 20 = ja-WP's vol-20 title and is OUR 184, inside v20 (180-189); (3) MangaDex's English feed carries the side story as a real installment and en-WP + MangaDex agree with OUR numbering from 123 on ('Disaster in the Finals!!' = 123, 'Zaboera's Son' = 124, 'The Fearsome Hyper Demon' = 125). NOTE that MangaDex is NOT usable as an anchor source for OUR 118-121: it numbers the side story 118 in its BUNKOBAN position (end of bunkoban vol 8), so its 119-122 are OUR 118-121; for OUR 118-121 the fandom and en-WP agree and MangaDex is +1. This block's chapters are all mainline and all verified in OUR space. || BLOCK MAP (OUR space): ep 30 = 104 (bulk), 105, 106, 107, 108 (partial), v12; ep 31 = 108 (bulk), 109, 110, 111 (partial), v12; ep 32 = 111 (partial), 112, 113, 114 (partial), v13; ep 33 = 114 (partial), 115, 116, 117, v13; ep 34 = 118, 119, 120, v13; ep 35 = 121, [122 = side story, skipped], 123, 124, 125 (partial), v14. || HANDOFFS: my first row, ep 30, OPENS on ch 104 — it holds that chapter's bulk while ep 29 (the 24-29 agent's last row) carries only its leading partial, so ep 29's END should be 104 and the two rows straddle it. My last row, ep 35, HANDS OFF inside OUR ch 125: ep 36 (the 36-41 agent's first row) starts on the remainder of 125 and runs to 129 (fandom's '124 (partial), 125, 126, 127, 128 (partial)' = OUR 125 (partial), 126, 127, 128, 129 (partial)). Every END is monotone (108 < 111 < 114 < 117 < 120 < 125) and sits above the lower fence ep 17 -> 60 [57] v7. || TYPES: all six rows are canon and stay canon; no filler, no recap segment, no anime-original block anywhere in 30-35 — the fandom's per-episode 'Manga differences' lists only alterations, extensions and cuts, which the faithfulness clause keeps canon. || ja-WP's 2020 各話リスト carries titles, dates and staff only — there is NO 原作 column on this series, so the independent instruments are en-WP's volume/chapter-title list, TV Tokyo's per-episode synopses (www.tv-tokyo.co.jp/anime/dai/episodes/, paginated: eps 31-40 on index_7.html, eps 21-30 on index_8.html) and MangaDex's chapter feed. The 2020 official site dq-dai.com is dead (S3 AccessDenied) and Bandai Channel's per-episode pages carry no synopsis text.

flags_for_sean: WAVE-LEVEL, ACT BEFORE LANDING w13d-w13g: the fandom's chapter numbering is ONE LOW relative to OUR space for every chapter from OUR 122 onward (the 122 slot is the bangaihen 'The Hero Avan' at the back of tankobon vol 13, which en-WP counts and the fandom does not). Sub-blocks 36-41, 42-47, 48-53 and 54-59 sit entirely above that line, and the batch-17 verdict's method (fandom forward + fandom reverse, with en-WP used only for namesake corroboration) does not surface the offset — an agent that copies a fandom number above 121 straight into an anchor will be one chapter low on EVERY row. Check each sibling file against the stored v-table before applying: a delivered END whose stored volume disagrees with the boundary table is the tell (anchor_volume_mismatch).

dragonquest.fandom ep-34 forward field is wrong in BOTH directions — it drops ch 118 and adds ch 121. I resolved it with the reverse fields plus TV Tokyo's synopses (118 in ep 34, 121 opening ep 35) and marked ep 34 medium. If Sean wants ep 34's END raised to 121 the evidence would have to come from a page-level read of ch 121's opening; nothing I found supports it.

dragonquest.fandom ch-112 reverse field reads 'adapted = 2020: episode 31 (Partial)' and names no episode that completes the chapter — a self-inconsistent field. The ep-31 and ep-32 forward fields and TV Tokyo's ep-32 synopsis put ch 112 whole in ep 32, so ep 31's END is 111 (medium). If instead ep 31 does reach into 112, ep 31's END becomes 112 and its continue moves to 112; nothing else in the block shifts.

A47 was not invoked anywhere in this block: three ENDs (30 -> 108, 32 -> 114, 35 -> 125) advance onto a chapter the next episode also starts on, and in each case the trailing share is story-carrying rather than a <=5-page or teaser-worded scrap (ep 31 opens on the crest already raised; ep 33 opens after the palace ultimatum has been shown; ep 36 opens on Zamza already transformed). No page counts are available for this series, and the series' stored convention from batch 17 (ep 12 -> 44 'opening only', ep 16 -> 57) advances the END the same way. If Sean wants A47 applied on wording alone, eps 30/32/35 are the three candidates and each would drop one chapter with a mandatory `partial` annotation.

Out of scope but adjacent: OUR total_chapters = 349 = 348 mainline tankobon chapters + the slot-122 side story. A Japanese secondary count (5 one-shots + 344 magazine installments, of which magazine 300 and 301 were merged into one tankobon chapter) also lands on 349 by a different route — the numbers agree but the composition does not, and the fandom's chapter pages stop before 299 so I could not test whether a SECOND break exists around OUR 300/301. Rows 30-35 are far below it; the wave-14 ep-100 MU pin (349) is where it would matter.
